messages:
sam: kicking off a quick convo about the sidecar-based minibatch coordinator PoC. goal: validate deadline dilution, prefetch benefit, and per-node fairness before any global control-plane work

tanvi: +1. can we scope the minimum viable API so clients don't have to change much?

sam: MVP API (very small):
```
request_token(window_hint_ms, tenant) -> token
use_token(token, batch_payload) -> result
release_token(token, reason) -> ok
metrics(token_id, event, value) -> ok
```

sam: token encodes TTL, deadline_ms, tenant_id, and a compact HMAC so sidecars can be dumb-validated

leo: thoughts on token ownership? i prefer tokens be ephemeral and stored in the sidecar process (no etcd) for PoC

tanvi: agree ephemeral lowers infra risk. downside: per-node fairness only, not cluster-wide — that's acceptable for initial experiment

olivia: how do clients behave if sidecar is slow/unavailable? we must avoid long tail blocking requests

sam: client policy: if token request doesn't return within X ms -> fallback immediately to degraded path (smaller model or no KV warmup). also record timeout counter per-tenant

leo: eviction rules? if KV eviction collides with an in-flight token, sidecar should annotate token with eviction_hint so downstream can opt out of heavy KV ops

olivia: prefetch hook is essential. prefetch(token) should attempt KV warm and return true/false — if false, caller can choose a cheaper path

tanvi: observability checklist:
- token_id in traces
- per-token latency histogram
- acquire/hold/release reasons labelled (deadline, eviction, prefetch-fail)
- tenant credit usage gauge

sam: also emit a simple CSV-style event for quick dashboarding:
`ts,token,phase,ms,tenant,reason` e.g. `1612345678,0xabc,acquire,12,team-x,ok`

leo: fairness: sidecar will keep a credit balance map tenant->credits and decrement on each acquire. credits are replenished by a local allocator tied to node capacity. not perfect but simple

olivia: what about small-request aggregation? two tiny requests could contend for the same KV slots once merged into a batch
tanvi: tie-breaker: token priority then FIFO sequence number then deterministic hash on tenant+seq to avoid oscillation

sam: failure scenario planning:
- sidecar crash mid-token: client times out and falls back; metric: token-orphaned++
- network partition: sidecar still serves local clients; cluster fairness lost but safe
- token replay/forgery: HMAC + TTL prevents this in private deployments

leo: rollout plan:
1) feature flag sidecar on dev nodes, enable for internal low-traffic tenants
2) collect 1 week of metrics, focus on acquire latency and prefetch hit rate
3) iterate on TTL and heartbeat heuristics
4) if stable, expand to more nodes and evaluate global coordinator tradeoffs

olivia: dashboards to add: per-tenant tail latency with and without tokens, prefetch success rate, token TTL expirations, token-orphaned counts

sam: perf targets for PoC: median acquire < 10ms, 95th < 50ms. prefetch should improve end-to-end tokenized request p95 by at least 10% for KV-heavy paths

tanvi: can we mock the prefetch failure mode in integration tests? need deterministic signal to simulate eviction and starvation

sam: yes — sidecar exposes a testing endpoint to inject prefetch=false for a token id. good for CI and manual runs

leo: security note: HMAC key rotation needed if sidecar tokens are consumed across boundaries. for PoC, single-node key + short TTL is fine

olivia: add a circuit-breaker at the client that trips after N consecutive token timeouts per tenant. when open, client uses degraded model for M minutes and retries slowly

sam: API ergonomics: keep token opaque to user SDKs, SDK just does `with_token(token): assemble_and_send()` so minimal code churn

canary-bot: canary launched: sidecar-batcher v0.1 -> nodeset "batch-proof-1" (5 nodes) :rocket:

tanvi: next owners: sam + leo implement sidecar, olivia wires dashboards and client breaker, i'll coordinate canary schedule and traffic split

sam: i'll draft a short RFC with API, metrics, and rollout checklist — will post here when ready

olivia: tiny note: add a debug endpoint returning current credits map + tokens so on-call can inspect quickly during canaries

sam: ack. let's keep the contract conservative: sidecar tells clients when to stop queuing (hard reject) and gives soft hints for shaping. no heuristic exposure from coordinator to callers

leo: final Q: long-term plan — if PoC looks promising we either (a) keep sidecars + global aggregator for cross-node fairness or (b) move token state to central store with lease semantics. both have tradeoffs; we'll decide after metrics

sam: thanks all. short action items in thread: implement PoC, add debug + test hooks, create dashboards, coordinate canary. I'll mark items in the RFC and link once done

tanvi: :thumbsup:
